sentences.zh: 你有一个新播客，是你和剧集联合主创克雷格·托马斯共同主持的，叫做《我们是如何创造你母亲的》。

sentences.en: It's a great podcaSt.

sentences.en: I've been listening.
sentences.zh: 我一直在听。

sentences.en: And one thing I wanted to ask you right up front.
sentences.zh: 有一件事我想一开始就问你。

sentences.en: In one of the first couple of episodes, you and Craig discuss How I Met Your Mother is a very puzzly show.
sentences.zh: 在前几集里，你和克雷格探讨了《老爸老妈浪漫史》是一部非常像解谜游戏的剧集。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little about in what ways is How I Met Your Mother puzzly?

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Well, when I got the show and people would ask me what it was and I would say it's almost like if Quentin Tarantino created a sitcom because it would go nonlinear and there were,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我接手这个节目时，如果有人问我是什么类型的，我会说它就像昆汀·塔伦蒂诺创作的情景喜剧，因为它采用非线性叙事，而且

sentences.en: you know, average of 40 to 60 scenes per episode all kind of scrambled and told out of order.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每集平均有40到60个场景，全都打乱顺序、不按时间来讲。

sentences.en: But the central premise of the show is this mystery.
sentences.zh: 但节目的核心设定其实是一个谜团。

sentences.en: You know, I my characters telling his kids in the year 2030 or 2035.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的角色在2030年或2035年向他的孩子们讲述。

sentences.en: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我记不清了。

sentences.en: I think it's 2030.
sentences.zh: 我想是2030年。

sentences.en: What, you know, the story, the long meandering story of how he met their mother.
sentences.zh: 讲述他是如何遇到他们的母亲的漫长而曲折的故事。

sentences.en: So they know who the mother is.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道母亲是谁。

sentences.en: The audience doesn't know who the mother is.
sentences.zh: 但观众不知道母亲是谁。

sentences.en: So the whole thing is structured as this mystery.
sentences.zh: 因此整部剧都围绕着这个谜团来构建。

sentences.en: We know that there's a there's a meeting at some point, but he's going to take his time and he's going to fill in all the details.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们最终会相遇，但他会不急不慢地把所有的细节都补全。

sentences.en: And sometimes individual episodes are structured as a mystery.
sentences.zh: 而且有时单集也会采用这种悬疑的结构。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of there's an episode called Ted Mosby Architect that it just looked like Ted was doing all these insane, slightly criminal things.
sentences.zh: 我想起有一集叫《建筑师泰德·莫斯比》，那一集里泰德做的事看起来疯狂又有点像犯罪。

sentences.en: And it was confusing.
sentences.zh: 让人一头雾水。

sentences.en: Like, why was he doing these?
sentences.zh: 比如，他为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: And then it's revealed it wasn't actually him.
sentences.zh: 然后剧情揭晓，其实那并不是他干的。

sentences.en: You know, there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是这样。

sentences.en: So I think Carter and Craig just had a taste for almost like an elegant withhold of information.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得卡特和克雷格只是喜欢那种优雅的信息保留手法。

sentences.en: And there was something very satisfying.
sentences.zh: 而且这种方式非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: One of the things we're interrogating in the show is why is the show maintained its level of popularity?
sentences.zh: 我们在这个节目中探讨的问题之一，就是为什么这部剧能一直保持这么高的热度？

sentences.en: Why is it minting new fans, you know, generation after generation?
sentences.zh: 为什么它能一代又一代地不断吸引新粉丝？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know if we can say generation after generation.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不知道能不能说是一代又一代。

sentences.en: It's been a lot of years since it went off.
sentences.zh: 毕竟距离它完结已经过去很多年了。

sentences.en: But I know a lot, you know, 12 year olds, teenagers, like they're discovering the show.
sentences.zh: 但我知道很多，你知道的，12岁的小孩、青少年，他们都开始迷上这部剧了。

sentences.en: And we're kind of investigating the mystery of the show.
sentences.zh: 我们也在探索这部剧的魅力之谜。

sentences.en: Why is the show inspire such loyalty and devotion?
sentences.zh: 为什么这部剧能激起如此强烈的忠诚和热爱？

sentences.en: And I think there's a lot of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 我想这背后有很多原因。

sentences.en: But one of them, I think, is it really keeps you on your toes.
sentences.zh: 但其中之一，我认为是它真的让你时刻保持专注。

sentences.en: I mean, it asks something of you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它对观众是有要求的。

sentences.en: You know, it's not it's not something that I mean, you can sit back and passively watch it, but it will also engage you in a kind of puzzly, fun way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它不是那种你只能坐着被动观看的剧，它会以一种充满趣味的解谜方式吸引你参与其中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, I love that.
sentences.zh: 噢，我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: I mean, there's the big puzzle of who the mother is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有关于母亲是谁的巨大谜团。

sentences.en: There's the famous episode called The Pineapple Incident.
sentences.zh: 还有那个著名的单集叫《菠萝悬案》。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 我正想提这个呢。

sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 那为什么叫“谜题”？

sentences.en: Among other luminaries on the, I think, Upper East Side, that episode.

sentences.zh: 而且有一件很奇怪的事情，你在一部长寿剧里待的时间越长，编剧们就会越来越了解你，然后他们就会开始“偷”一点东西。

sentences.en: They start stealing from your life and throwing things into the character.

sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会注意到乔什的名字“Josh”，同时也是一个动词，意思是开玩笑、逗弄。

sentences.en: Well, here at the Puzzler, we notice that two of the other How I Met Your Mother co-stars
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在谜题节目注意到，《老爸老妈浪漫史》另外两位联合主演

sentences.en: also have names that are verbs or at least sound like verbs.
sentences.zh: 的名字也是动词，或者听起来像动词。

sentences.en: They are spelled slightly differently, but they are homophones.
sentences.zh: 它们的拼写略有不同，但它们是同音词。

sentences.en: So our question is, can you name these other two co-stars and their verb sound-alike first or last names,
sentences.zh: 所以我们的问题是，你能说出这两位联合主演以及他们听起来像动词的名字或姓氏吗？

sentences.en: the answers, and more puzzling goodness after the break.
sentences.zh: 答案以及更多烧脑好玩的谜题，广告之后揭晓。

sentences.en: Hello, Puzzlers.
sentences.zh: 大家好，谜题迷们。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the Puzzler, the plucky orphan in your Puzzle Dickens novel.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到谜题节目，也就是你那部谜题狄更斯小说里那个勇敢的孤儿。

sentences.en: I'm your host, AJ Jacobs, and I'm here with Chief Puzzle Officer Greg Pliska.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人AJ·雅各布斯，和我在一起的是首席谜题官格雷格·普利斯卡。

sentences.en: Greg, before the break, we asked about the co-stars of How I Met Your Mother.
sentences.zh: 格雷格，在休息之前，我们问了关于《老爸老妈浪漫史》联合主演的问题。

sentences.en: Which of them have names that sound like verbs?
sentences.zh: 他们当中有谁的名字听起来像动词？

sentences.en: Any good.
sentences.zh: 有什么好主意吗。

sentences.en: Well, one is the guy with the hard-to-identify hair color.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个是那个头发颜色很难界定的家伙。

sentences.en: Good point.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: Neil Patrick Harris.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·帕特里克·哈里斯。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是他。

sentences.en: And his first name?
sentences.zh: 他的名呢？

sentences.en: Neil.
sentences.zh: 尼尔。

sentences.en: Neil.
sentences.zh: 尼尔。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sounds like Neil.
sentences.zh: 听起来像跪下（Kneel）。

sentences.en: Also, wasn't the narrator on the show Bob Saget, like bobbing for apples?
sentences.zh: 还有，剧中的旁白不是鲍勃·萨吉特吗，就像bobbing for apples（水盆咬苹果游戏）里的bob？

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, good point.
sentences.zh: 对，说得好。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And by the way, though, we're not done with Neil Patrick Harris because his last name sounds a little like harass.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们还没讲完尼尔·帕特里克·哈里斯，因为他的姓听起来有点像骚扰（Harass）。
zh_words: 完尼尔·帕特里克·哈里斯

sentences.en: Well, some people pronounce that word Harris.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人把那个词发音成哈里斯（Harris）。

sentences.en: Right, like sort of more British, which is what his character, Barney Stinson, excels at.
sentences.zh: 对，有点像更地道的英式发音，这也是他的角色巴尼·斯廷森最擅长的。

sentences.en: He is a harasser.
sentences.zh: 他是个烦人精。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: What about, no, I was going to say Coby Smulders.
sentences.zh: 或者说，不，我本想说科比·史莫德斯。

sentences.en: Smulders sounds a little bit like smulders, but that doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 史莫德斯听起来有点像闷烧，但那样行不通。

sentences.en: Not just a little.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是一点点。

sentences.en: I think it works totally.
sentences.zh: 我觉得完全行得通。

sentences.en: It is very, it's hard to say smulders and smolders, smolders.
sentences.zh: 这确实很……很难同时说好史莫德斯和闷烧。

sentences.en: You just said them differently.
sentences.zh: 你刚才分明读得不一样。

sentences.en: They're two different things.
sentences.zh: 那是两码事。

sentences.en: I still count.
sentences.zh: 我依然觉得算数。

sentences.en: It's smolders and burn slowly.
sentences.zh: 一个是史莫德斯，另一个是慢慢燃烧。

sentences.en: Obviously, we have.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们有。

sentences.en: I want to make a case for Coby.
sentences.zh: 我想为科比争取一下。

sentences.en: I want to make a case for Coby.
sentences.zh: 我想为科比争取一下。

sentences.en: My son, every time he takes a wadded up thing of paper and tosses it across the room into the garbage can, says, Coby.
sentences.zh: 我儿子每次把一团揉皱的纸扔过房间进垃圾桶时，都会说：“科比。”

sentences.en: Now, he's referencing the great Coby Bryant, of course, but it's almost like it's a verb.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是在致敬伟大的科比·布莱恩特，但这几乎成了一个动词。

sentences.en: I'm going to Coby that into the garbage can.
sentences.zh: 我要把那个“科比”进垃圾桶里。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Listen.
sentences.zh: 听着。

sentences.en: I mean, if you could have smolders, smolders, I can have Coby.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既然你能有闷烧，那我也可以有科比。

sentences.en: I think yours is a little more of a stretch, but I will give it to you because I am very liberal.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的有点太勉强了，不过我很大度，就算你过了。

sentences.en: I will say we have another that's a noun.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我们还有另一个名词。

sentences.en: It's not that we got Jason Siegel.
sentences.zh: 倒不是因为我们请到了杰森·席格尔。

sentences.en: Kind of sounds like Jonathan Livington Siegel.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像乔纳森·利文斯顿·席格尔。
zh_words: 乔纳森·利文斯顿·席格尔

sentences.en: It's not a verb, but it's a noun.
sentences.zh: 这不是个动词，但它是个名词。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, enough wordplay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不管怎样，文字游戏就到这里。

sentences.en: I bring all this up because we have more wordplay to do with our guest this week, none other than Josh Radner.
sentences.zh: 我提起这些是因为我们本周的嘉宾身上还有更多文字游戏可玩，他不是别人，正是乔什·拉德纳。

sentences.en: He is an actor, filmmaker, musician, podcaster, and star of the above mentioned How I Met Your Mother.
sentences.zh: 他是一位演员、电影制作人、音乐人、播客主持人，也是前面提到的《老爸老妈浪漫史》的主演。

sentences.en: Welcome, Josh.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，乔什。

sentences.en: Hi, AJ.
sentences.zh: 嗨，AJ。

sentences.en: It's good to be here again.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能再次来到这里。

sentences.en: We are delighted to have you back and to celebrate your new podcast,
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴你能重返节目，并庆祝你的新播客，

sentences.en: what you're doing with How I Met Your Mother co-creator, Craig Thomas, called How We Made Your Mother,
sentences.zh: 也就是你和《老爸老妈浪漫史》联合创作者克雷格·托马斯合作的节目，名叫《我们是如何创造你老妈的》，

sentences.en: which is very puzzly.
sentences.zh: 这名字非常有解谜感。

sentences.en: We like that kind of a wordplay.
sentences.zh: 我们很喜欢这种文字游戏。

sentences.en: So I am actually also have someone I do the podcast with, and his name is Greg Pliska.
sentences.zh: 所以其实我和一个一起做播客的人合作，他的名字叫格雷格·普利斯卡。

sentences.en: So I am going to turn.
sentences.zh: 所以我要转到……

sentences.en: That's my segue.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的过渡。

sentences.en: Turn it over to Greg because he has a puzzle for you today.
sentences.zh: 交给格雷格，因为他今天给你准备了一个谜题。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Actually, I have a question, Josh, which is, have you watched, are you guys, are you watching every minute of every episode as you do the podcast?
sentences.zh: 事实上，乔什，我有个问题，那就是你们在做播客时，是不是把每一集的每一分钟都看了一遍？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm watching, well, the impetus for the show is actually, I got married a little over a year ago, and my wife had never seen a single episode of the show.
sentences.zh: 对，我在看，其实节目的契机是，我一年多前刚结婚，我妻子以前从没看过这剧的任何一集。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, she really wanted to watch it, and I thought, well, this is probably a good time for me to rewatch it because I haven't seen a lot of those episodes in 20,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，既然她真的很想看，我觉得这大概也是我重温的好时机，因为其中很多集我已经20年没看过啦，

sentences.en: 15 years.
And I didn't even watch every episode when they came out.
sentences.zh: 而且当年播出的时候我甚至都没看过每一集。

sentences.en: I had a somewhat conflicted relationship with watching myself at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时我对在屏幕上看到自己有着一种矛盾的心态。

sentences.en: I'm finding it easier now with some distance.
sentences.zh: 现在有了一段距离，我发现看的时候轻松多了。

sentences.en: Oh, and I should say, AJ, it's just, my wife shares your last name.
sentences.zh: 哦，我得说，AJ，真巧，我妻子跟你同一个姓。

sentences.en: My wife is a Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 我妻子也姓雅各布斯。

sentences.en: I saw that.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.en: So we are probably somewhat related by marriage at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上讲，我们现在可能算是有亲戚关系了。

sentences.en: We're cousins.
sentences.zh: 我们是表亲。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这样了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so then I reached out to Craig, and I said, you know, I'm going to rewatch the show.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，所以后来我联系了克雷格，我说，你知道的，我打算重温这部剧。

sentences.en: If he wanted to formalize it and do something on the record, I think it could be really fun to talk about the show.
sentences.zh: 如果他想把这事正式化，录点什么公开的内容，我觉得聊聊这部剧会非常有趣。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这样了。

sentences.en: And I also am excited because I know your wife, is it a psychologist?
sentences.zh: 而且我也很兴奋，因为我认识你妻子，她是个心理学家吗？

sentences.en: She's a clinical psychologist, yeah.
sentences.zh: 她是一名临床心理学家，对。

sentences.en: Clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 临床心理学家。

sentences.en: So is she going to be weighing in with some insights on the psychology of these characters?
sentences.zh: 那她会从这些角色的心理学角度发表一些见解吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 会的。

sentences.en: We actually have a special section called Questions and Observations from a clinical psychologist and relationship expert who's never seen the show,
sentences.zh: 我们其实有一个特别板块，叫做“来自临床心理学家兼亲密关系专家的提问与观察”，她以前从没看过这部剧，

sentences.en: who also happens to be married to John.
sentences.zh: 而且恰好还是约翰的妻子。

sentences.en: Catchy.
sentences.zh: 真上口。

sentences.en: We don't have an opportunity for it yet.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还没想好它的名字。

sentences.en: Maybe you can help me figure it out.
sentences.zh: 也许你能帮我想想。

sentences.en: But I'd say every two episodes, she records a voice note from her office once she's collected her thoughts after watching the episode.
sentences.zh: 不过我想大概每看两集，她看完后在办公室整理好思绪，就会录下一段语音。

sentences.en: And they're really deep-searching, interesting questions and observations.
sentences.zh: 那些都是非常深入、有趣的提问和观察。

sentences.en: So it really takes it a notch deeper for us.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实让我们的节目更有深度了。

sentences.en: Is she able to come up with a diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 她能给出诊断结果吗？

sentences.en: Or something like Barney, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 或者像巴尼那种情况。

sentences.en: Well, we have been talking a bit about Ted's attachment disorder, his anxious attachment and Robin's avoidant attachment style.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实聊过一些关于特德的依恋障碍、他的焦虑型依恋，以及罗宾回避型的依恋风格。

sentences.en: So that wasn't in vogue when we were doing the show, but it absolutely lines up with where the kind of psychology.
sentences.zh: 当年我们拍这部剧时，这还不那么流行，但它完全符合现在的心理学方向。

sentences.en: Oh, last question about watching it with your wife.
sentences.zh: 哦，关于和你妻子一起看的最后一个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, are you sitting next to her on the couch and are you able to watch the show or do you watch her watching the show?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你是坐在她身边的沙发上一起看剧，还是在一旁观察她看剧？

sentences.en: I actually have to watch the show because I need to discuss it with some, you know, authority.
sentences.zh: 我其实必须得看剧，因为我得带着点权威性跟别人讨论它。

sentences.en: So I've been watching it, but I'm very tuned into what delights her.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在看，但我对什么能取悦她非常敏感。

sentences.en: You know, I'm very keyed into when she audibly laughs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她什么时候出声大笑，我都听得一清二楚。
